$comment: High-intent query detection for `npm run insights` (scripts/lib/intent.mjs). A Search Console query is HIGH-INTENT when it reads like a buyer choosing, not a reader learning: it carries one of the `signals` (software, system, tool, pricing, vs, …) or sits on the `watch` list. Navigational brand queries are excluded by `navigational`. These rows are printed FIRST in every insights pull and worked first in every cadence run (content-cadence step 2) — on a zero-click site they sit far below the informational rows by volume, and a run that reads the report top-down never reaches them. `claimFrom` names the collections whose entries declare `primaryKeyword`/`secondaryKeywords` in frontmatter (the money pages): the report cross-checks the page Google shows a query on against the page that claims it and flags `wrong-page` / `unmapped`. `watch` is curated by a human or the weekly keyword-map refresh — the transactional phrasings the site means to win, each tied to the page that claims it, so a zero-impression term is reported as 'not showing yet' instead of silently absent.
$bofuComment: Bottom-of-funnel SHAPES, on top of the signal words: a query that matches one of these regexes is a buyer comparing, switching or shortlisting, whatever its volume. `npm run insights` prints every such row at position 4–20 as its own block (the quickest leads from search sit at positions 1–5, and a BOFU row at 4–20 is the cheapest one to move). Each entry: a label the report prints and a case-insensitive regex source. `<competitor>` expands to the alternation of `competitors` below; a pattern that needs it is skipped while that list is empty.
$competitorsComment: The rivals the buyer compares this site with, as they are spelled in queries (lower-case, no punctuation): from marketing/landscape.md. A Search Console query naming one of them is printed in its own block (`competitorQueries`) and expands the `<competitor>` BOFU shapes above. Reviewed monthly (ACTIONS A-M03); a name is added the month it appears in a SERP or a prompt-panel answer. Empty = no competitor rows, no `<competitor>` shapes.
$quickWinsComment: The quickest keyword optimisation there is: a page already shown at position ≤ `quickWins.maxPosition` for a query it does not literally say. Adding the phrase to a heading, the description or a FAQ line is the cheapest ranking move on the board. Printed by `npm run insights` from the page × query rows against each page's SOURCE (scripts/lib/pageText.mjs).
$navigationalComment: TODO — your own brand name and its common misspellings, plus other products' names that land on your pages by accident (a query that is somebody else's brand is noise, not a buyer). Filled by /onboard-marketing or by hand; the weekly cadence run adds what the snapshots turn up.
$claimFromComment: The collections whose entries carry `primaryKeyword` (+ `secondaryKeywords`) frontmatter — the money pages. The report cross-checks the page Google shows a query on against the page that claims it. Both collections below require `primaryKeyword` in their schema, so every entry in them claims exactly one query. Add a row for any further collection a site gives that field to; a collection listed here with no entries simply contributes none, which is the state this template ships in.
$watchComment: TODO — one object per transactional phrasing the site means to win: { "query": "<exact words a buyer types>", "page": "/<route that claims it>", "since": "YYYY-MM-DD", "note": "<why it is here, what was done>" }. Add a term the day it first earns an impression (or the day a competitor sweep shows a rival owns it); never retire one — a term that stopped showing is a finding, not noise. Keep `page` in step with that page's frontmatter keywords and with marketing/keyword-map.md § High-intent, in the same commit.
